mission.title: The Caretaker
mission.description: Learn where the interface program's human host is held from a Zionite's access card, then get Persephone to a Machine terminal to free it.

npc.say:
Ehh... You know it will be dangerous, my dear. But, if you are really determined to take this rash step...
Yes? Es-tu sure? Well, then we will do it.
{player}, contact Flood. He will guide you to the Machine terminal you must secure for my wife.
Do as my husband tells you.

She has always been headstrong, but this--! It is going too far. What will they say of me if my wife gets herself killed so, hm?
Non, non... She is forgetting her responsibilities. Hmh...

phase.briefing:
Hmph. Seraph didn't get away...we let him go. Dreadfully boring fellow; never has anything to say for himself, anyway. Was worth it to give those Zionites a thrashing in Mara, though.
Now, {player}, to the business of the day: while Seraph was the center of attention in Mara, that interface program slipped away, and appears to have got itself into the actual body of a human. Why it would voluntarily go into the Machine pod system, I have no idea; I always did think it was a few bits short.
The Machines have the human--Imelda Kroller--under obscenely heavy guard, but word has it that a Zionite ran into Wright before that, and she foolishly shot her mouth off about Kroller's pod. If we can find her pod, we can see about getting that interface program out of it. You're going after the Zionite.

enter.say: Okay, the Zionite who ran into Wright earlier should be in there. Let's see if we can find out what Wright said about the pod.

objective.text: Take the access card from the Zionite

done.say: They were carrying an access card, huh? Could be handy.
Serial number for the bluepill, eh? Let's get a check run on that.

near.say: Oh, please. I don't have time for this.

phase.briefing:
That's Machine pod serial number format, operative; I thought everyone knew that. The third number is the pod's ring on the tower, so evidently Wright detected the interface program in the one hundred and forty ninth ring, and began hunting down all the humans she could find connected to it.
Wright may have to flail around with brute force approaches, but when it comes to knowing the pod system inside and out, we're the real experts. Now that we know the program's approximate position in the pod network, you'll find that the Merovingian can locate it like that.
Oh, for... Just imagine you could hear me snap my fingers, then.

enter.say: There was that thing a little while after the Truce broke where we were checking out why a woman named MacHenry had just up and vanished from her pod, and we swiped the logs of the Machine caretaker droid in charge of the pod. Maybe we can do that again to find this Kroller chick.

talk.say: Yes, we'll hack into their system, and locate the caretaker for those pods. There should be some record of the progra--

done.say:
No. That will only give us information; it will not save the woman--or the program. You think the Machines can protect them? That monster will take everything.
Get me a connection to that part of the Machine network. I will find them. I will save them.

Ehh... You know it will be dangerous, my dear. But, if you are really determined to take this rash step...
Yes? Es-tu sure? Well, then we will do it.
{player}, contact Flood. He will guide you to the Machine terminal you must secure for my wife.

near.say: She's been a moody one, hm?
Keep your mind on your work, brother.

phase.briefing: I'm not one to judge, operative... Well, she is behaving foolishly. You, however, had better wrap your inelastic mind around the task at hand: you've got a Machine control terminal to commandeer.

enter.say:
Persephone was a caretaker herself before she went into Exile, so I guess she must know what she's doing...
Okay, the terminal we need is in there. I'm reading a lot of program activity in there, so watch out.

objective.text: Clear the programs from the terminal

done.say: Okay, they've brought Persephone in. She's in a room nearby.

talk.say:
Take me to the computer, now!
If we are too late...

done.say: Get her to that computer. And no funny business with trying to take her outside!

Holy-- The Machines must've been watching that system; she had defense routines all over her as soon as she sent the commands.
Oh, man; her signal is not looking good. The Merv's gonna kill us for sure.
Unh... I have done it... They are safe...

phase.briefing: Oh, no; I'm not taking the heat for this one. It was her idea, and you were the one there with her. You go explain it to the Merovingian.

enter.say: Well, hey...at least she isn't dead.; they're telling me she was still alive when they got her back to the chateau, anyway.

talk.say:
Yes, yes, my wife; I have heard. ... I warned her, did I not? Et, she must have known about those defense routines, but she said nothing... If she had asked for my help, I would have given it, of course!
But, enough; she has liberated the program from the hands of our enemies. We must move swiftly to take advantage of this.

near.say: Hm... No, I don't remember anyone letting the boss' wife get hacked almost to death before. I wonder what he'll do.

They detected it on their way back: the wreckage of a compact craft, similar to those that attacked them in the no-fly zone. Among the pieces, my men found an inert but mostly intact android. It does not match any known type. They're bringing it with them now.

mission.finish:
Bah, all she managed to do was to restart Kroller's RSI at a random point in the simulation. Now, who do you suppose is going to have to go collect her?
Oh, I don't know. I'll get back to you later, {player}; I'm busy.
